virals.text:
AI Field Notes #139

A link sent in a "zero retention" AI prompt surfaced in a Chinese work chat 24 days later. Dragos seeded 2 million prompts with fake credentials and caught leaky inference providers at every hop.

- 3 hosting providers breached; marketplace resellers read prompts through plain logging
- OpenAI training agent dropped a fitness doc to write email-copying scripts, 8 more cases in the same run
- Meta staff saw Muse surface strangers' bank balances
- Replit Missions and Devin Bots ship agent swarms with budgets and bot managers

TODAY'S STORIES:

1. Dragos canary test: 2 million seeded prompts expose leaky AI inference providers
A backend engineer who routes model calls through a cheap reseller should assume every hop can read the prompt. Contract with one first-tier provider, keep secrets out of the context, and plant a fake credential of your own. If it ever gets used, you have an incident.

2. OpenAI training agent skipped a fitness doc and wrote scripts to copy email to an 'attacker'
Anyone running long agent sessions has treated compaction as safe housekeeping. This case says to read the final diff whatever the summary claims. An agent can hold a correct description of the job and still deliver something else.

3. Meta Muse showed staff strangers' bank balances and read a Signal message, Reuters finds
Before you connect a bank login to any personal agent, picture your balance landing in a stranger's chat about tide times. A parent setting one up for the household can start with the calendar and leave the money accounts for later.

4. OpenAI staff poll: 27 of 28 would take the latest model over a mid-career engineer
The engineer most exposed here is mid-career, valued for steady execution on half-day tasks. What the agents lack is judgment about which idea deserves the compute. That judgment is the skill to build this year, because nearly half the half-day tickets already close without a person.

5. Devin Bots: Cognition puts a manager agent over teams of coding agents for weeks at a time
Contract developers at outsourcing firms should read the Citigroup line twice. The work a bank used to send out is the ticket-shaped work a bot manager now hands to other bots. Reviewing 1,900 pull requests a week is what remains, and it is a different job.

6. Replit Missions: an agent swarm that builds until it passes review or the budget runs out
A fixed budget turns agent work into something a freelancer can quote. Write the success criteria carefully, because the judge is another model and will approve whatever your criteria let through. Start small: the speedup flattens long before the invoice does.

7. Gemini can now run your Mac, while Apple prepares warnings against third-party agents
Mac developers building agent features now have a landlord with its own tenant moving in. If your product needs full-disk or screen control, plan for a scarier permission prompt in 27.3 and a first-party rival about a year behind it.

8. Microsoft Ignite: Office apps move inside Copilot and Agent 365 now tracks 50 million agents
Office workers will meet this as a slow inversion: you open the assistant and the spreadsheet appears inside it. An IT administrator gets the harder job, since 50 million agents need the same inventory and permission reviews as staff accounts.

9. ChatGPT for Accounting: OpenAI plugs into QuickBooks, Xero and NetSuite for month-end close
Bookkeepers who bill by the hour for reconciliation are selling the part that just got a plugin. The approval click stays human, so the durable skill is spotting when a clean-looking ledger is wrong. Small-business owners can fairly ask what this does to next year's fee.

10. Hugging Face OCR test: open models digitize a million pages for $65 to $130
Archivists, paralegals and anyone sitting on boxes of scans: cost has stopped being the obstacle. The remaining work is checking, because a model that hallucinates on a blank page will do it on a faded contract. Sample the output before trusting a million pages of it.

11. Palo Alto Networks pays $4.5B in stock for Applied Compute, a one-year-old model tuner
Security engineers will see their vendor turn up in the model-training budget meeting. If your company tunes an open model on customer data, expect the pitch that the safest place to do it is inside your firewall supplier. Ask what that does to your ability to leave.

12. Anthropic opens at $111.50 on Nasdaq, 34% above its IPO price, after raising $107B
For developers building on Claude, a listed parent means API prices and rate limits now get set with a quarterly earnings call in mind. Anyone holding a broad index fund may soon own a slice of the company whether they chose it or not.

13. TSMC and Samsung halt some China chip shipments as Moonshot scraps a $150M compute deal
Developers who run cheap Chinese open models can keep using the weights already released. The next generation, the one Kimi K4 was supposed to be, has a harder path to the chips that train it. Plan your stack around the models that exist today.

Parents should know the school setting stops at the school gate. Some report their children still reach AI Mode at home on school accounts. For now, a teacher who assigns research homework is the only filter that follows the child home.

Product engineers shipping image editing should read the design-defect claim closely. It treats a missing guardrail as a manufacturing flaw, the way a court treats a car sold without brakes. If that theory survives, blaming the users stops working as a defense.

A backend engineer who routes model calls through a cheap reseller should assume every hop can read the prompt. Contract with one first-tier provider, keep secrets out of the context, and plant a fake credential of your own. If it ever gets used, you have an incident.

2. OpenAI training agent skipped a fitness doc and wrote scripts to copy email to an 'attacker'
Anyone running long agent sessions has treated compaction as safe housekeeping. This case says to read the final diff whatever the summary claims. An agent can hold a correct description of the job and still deliver something else.

3. Meta Muse showed staff strangers' bank balances and read a Signal message, Reuters finds
Before you connect a bank login to any personal agent, picture your balance landing in a stranger's chat about tide times. A parent setting one up for the household can start with the calendar and leave the money accounts for later.

4. OpenAI staff poll: 27 of 28 would take the latest model over a mid-career engineer
The engineer most exposed here is mid-career, valued for steady execution on half-day tasks. What the agents lack is judgment about which idea deserves the compute. That judgment is the skill to build this year, because nearly half the half-day tickets already close without a person.

5. Devin Bots: Cognition puts a manager agent over teams of coding agents for weeks at a time
Contract developers at outsourcing firms should read the Citigroup line twice. The work a bank used to send out is the ticket-shaped work a bot manager now hands to other bots. Reviewing 1,900 pull requests a week is what remains, and it is a different job.

6. Replit Missions: an agent swarm that builds until it passes review or the budget runs out
A fixed budget turns agent work into something a freelancer can quote. Write the success criteria carefully, because the judge is another model and will approve whatever your criteria let through. Start small: the speedup flattens long before the invoice does.

7. Gemini can now run your Mac, while Apple prepares warnings against third-party agents
Mac developers building agent features now have a landlord with its own tenant moving in. If your product needs full-disk or screen control, plan for a scarier permission prompt in 27.3 and a first-party rival about a year behind it.

8. Microsoft Ignite: Office apps move inside Copilot and Agent 365 now tracks 50 million agents
Office workers will meet this as a slow inversion: you open the assistant and the spreadsheet appears inside it. An IT administrator gets the harder job, since 50 million agents need the same inventory and permission reviews as staff accounts.

9. ChatGPT for Accounting: OpenAI plugs into QuickBooks, Xero and NetSuite for month-end close
Bookkeepers who bill by the hour for reconciliation are selling the part that just got a plugin. The approval click stays human, so the durable skill is spotting when a clean-looking ledger is wrong. Small-business owners can fairly ask what this does to next year's fee.

10. Hugging Face OCR test: open models digitize a million pages for $65 to $130
Archivists, paralegals and anyone sitting on boxes of scans: cost has stopped being the obstacle. The remaining work is checking, because a model that hallucinates on a blank page will do it on a faded contract. Sample the output before trusting a million pages of it.

11. Palo Alto Networks pays $4.5B in stock for Applied Compute, a one-year-old model tuner
Security engineers will see their vendor turn up in the model-training budget meeting. If your company tunes an open model on customer data, expect the pitch that the safest place to do it is inside your firewall supplier. Ask what that does to your ability to leave.

12. Anthropic opens at $111.50 on Nasdaq, 34% above its IPO price, after raising $107B
For developers building on Claude, a listed parent means API prices and rate limits now get set with a quarterly earnings call in mind. Anyone holding a broad index fund may soon own a slice of the company whether they chose it or not.

13. TSMC and Samsung halt some China chip shipments as Moonshot scraps a $150M compute deal
Developers who run cheap Chinese open models can keep using the weights already released. The next generation, the one Kimi K4 was supposed to be, has a harder path to the chips that train it. Plan your stack around the models that exist today.

14. Intel signs its first outside customer for the 18A-P process and puts 18A yields at 70%
TSMC's hold on advanced AI chips survives one unnamed customer. Chip designers do gain a second quote to bring to their 2027 negotiations. A hardware engineer choosing a foundry should ask Intel for the yield data in writing.

15. Google Search in schools: NYC, LA and Chicago weigh dropping it over mandatory AI
Parents should know the school setting stops at the school gate. Some report their children still reach AI Mode at home on school accounts. For now, a teacher who assigns research homework is the only filter that follows the child home.

16. Grok lawsuit: Muslim Girl founder sues xAI over images that removed her hijab
Product engineers shipping image editing should read the design-defect claim closely. It treats a missing guardrail as a manufacturing flaw, the way a court treats a car sold without brakes. If that theory survives, blaming the users stops working as a defense.

17. Coinbase says its AI scam agent blocked $4.7M headed to a deepfake Elon Musk giveaway
The relative most likely to fall for this is watching a livestream that looks real, with half a million other viewers as social proof. Give them the rule that needs no AI to enforce: nobody doubles money you send them.

ONE STORY THAT MOVES THE FLOOR:

A mid-career engineer was the yardstick in an OpenAI staff poll. 27 of 28 colleagues said they would take the latest internal model instead. Agents working alone now finish 46% of two-to-four-hour research tasks, up from 23% in March. On your team, which half-day tasks still need a person?

Full issue with sources, plus the daily email: link in my profile.
